content:
No, penguins cannot fly in the air. While they are birds, their wings have evolved into flippers that make them excellent swimmers instead of flyers. 

However, penguins are sometimes described as "flying" underwater - they use their powerful flippers to propel themselves through water with incredible speed and agility, reaching speeds up to 22 mph (35 km/h). Their streamlined bodies and wing movements underwater look remarkably similar to birds flying through the air!

So while penguins are flightless birds on land and in air, they're master "flyers" in their underwater world.
